events.factual_description: DC Jazz Festival's current event page lists DC JazzFest Downtown at Anthem Row, 800 K Street NW in Washington, DC, on Thursday, September 3, 2026 from 4:30 PM to 8:00 PM, with Butcher Brown, Corcoran Holt, and Marshall Keys & Soulful Path. The event is free, with an optional suggested donation supporting DC Jazz Festival education programs. A recent DC Jazz Festival announcement independently confirms the same September 3 Anthem Row bill, describes Butcher Brown as jazz-funk favorites, identifies Corcoran Holt as a DC native, and calls Marshall Keys a legendary DC saxophonist. Individual artist set times and a detailed personnel roster for each billed act are not published on the verified pages, so none are inferred.

en.why_it_matters: This works as more than a free festival sampler because the bill puts three related Mid-Atlantic currents in the same downtown frame: Butcher Brown's elastic jazz-funk language, Corcoran Holt's DC-rooted bass voice, and Marshall Keys' long saxophone presence in the city's scene. The point is the local groove ecology and the public setting, not festival prestige by itself.
en.trip_verdict: If Thursday afternoon is open in the DMV, this is an easy one to fold into the day and worth arriving in time to hear the whole bill. Treat it as a strong local opportunity rather than a reason to reorganize travel around downtown DC.

es.why_it_matters: Esto funciona como algo más que una probadita gratuita de festival porque el cartel junta tres corrientes emparentadas del Mid-Atlantic en el mismo espacio del centro: el lenguaje elástico de jazz-funk de Butcher Brown, la voz de bajo de Corcoran Holt con raíces en DC y la presencia de Marshall Keys como saxofonista de larga trayectoria en la escena de la ciudad. Lo que importa es esa ecología local de groove y el contexto público, no el prestigio del festival por sí solo.
es.trip_verdict: Si el jueves por la tarde está libre en el DMV, es muy fácil incorporarlo al día y vale llegar con tiempo para escuchar el cartel completo. Lo trataría como una buena oportunidad local, no como razón para reorganizar un viaje alrededor del centro de DC.
